## ADR-001: Split utils.js into topic modules behind a re-export index

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-08-10
- Context: `src/utils.js` was a single grab-bag module holding string, array, and
  date helpers side by side. The groups share no code and change for unrelated
  reasons, so every edit touched the same file and the topical `// ----- x -----`
  comment banners were the only structure. External callers (and the test suite)
  depend on the flat `require('../src/utils.js')` surface, which must not change.
- Decision: Move each group into its own module — `src/strings.js`
  (`slugify`, `truncate`, `capitalize`), `src/arrays.js` (`chunk`, `unique`,
  `groupBy`), `src/dates.js` (`formatDate`, `daysBetween`, plus the `DAY_MS`
  constant that only date code used). `src/utils.js` becomes a pure index that
  re-exports the eight names explicitly, with no logic of its own.
  Function bodies were moved verbatim; this refactor changes no behaviour.
  The re-export list is written out name by name rather than spread from the
  submodules, so the public surface is stated in one readable place and a new
  helper is only public once someone adds it there deliberately.
- Consequences: New callers can depend on the narrow module they need
  (`require('./dates.js')`) instead of pulling in the whole grab-bag, and each
  topic has an obvious home for future helpers. The cost is one extra
  indirection when navigating from `utils.js` to an implementation, and the
  export list now exists in two places (submodule and index) — the API-surface
  test in `tests/utils.test.js` guards the index against drift.
- Alternatives considered: (a) leave the monolith and rely on the comment
  banners — rejected, the file only grows; (b) delete `utils.js` and have
  callers import the topic modules directly — rejected, it breaks the public
  API this task requires keeping intact; (c) build the index with
  `Object.assign`/spread over the submodules — rejected, it makes the public
  surface implicit and would silently re-export anything added downstream.

content.text:
Done — the split is committed and the suite is green.

## What changed

`src/utils.js` is now a pure index; the helpers live in three topic modules:

| Module | Exports |
|---|---|
| `src/strings.js` | `slugify`, `truncate`, `capitalize` |
| `src/arrays.js` | `chunk`, `unique`, `groupBy` |
| `src/dates.js` | `formatDate`, `daysBetween` (+ the `DAY_MS` constant, which only date code used) |

`src/utils.js:13-22` re-exports the eight names explicitly rather than spreading the submodules — the public surface stays stated in one readable place, and a new helper only becomes public when someone adds it there on purpose.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 15/15 pass, same as the baseline I ran before touching anything.
- `git diff -- tests/` is empty — no test was edited, skipped, or relaxed.
- I diffed every moved function against `git show HEAD:src/utils.js`: all 8 bodies are byte-identical, so this is a move, not a rewrite.

## Also

- ADR-001 appended to `team/DECISIONS.md` (context, decision, consequences, and the three alternatives I rejected — including deleting `utils.js` outright, which would have broken the API you asked to keep).
- Added a `.gitignore` for `node_modules/` and `.artifacts/`; the repo had none, and my verification scratch files needed somewhere to go per the working agreement.

Nothing is blocked and nothing is left uncommitted. One thing worth your call: the modules are `require`-able directly (`require('./dates.js')`), but nothing enforces that new helpers get added to the index — the API-surface test will fail loudly if the index drifts, which is the guard I relied on rather than adding machinery.
